Community Literacy Collaborative is a nonprofit organization dedicated to strengthening family literacy and early reading in underserved neighborhoods. For more than a decade, we have partnered with schools, libraries, and community organizations to deliver programs that help parents build the skills and confidence to support their children's reading at home.

Our leadership and staff bring direct experience in family coaching, early literacy programming, and program evaluation. The Program Manager (0.3 FTE) has managed multi-year grant-funded programs serving similar populations, including oversight of partner agreements, staff supervision, and funder reporting. The Evaluation Coordinator (0.4 FTE) has experience designing and managing pre/post evaluation frameworks, data-sharing agreements with school districts, and quarterly outcome reporting. Our two part-time Circle Facilitators are trained in dialogic reading techniques and peer-led group facilitation, and our two part-time Family Coaches bring experience in home visiting, parent coaching, and attendance follow-up. Together, this team has the skills and capacity to deliver every component of Family Literacy Circles, from weekly peer circles and biweekly coaching to data collection and quarterly reporting.

Our track record supports this confidence. Through prior programming, we have demonstrated improvements in family reading time and attendance among participating K–3 students. We have experience administering parent surveys, collecting and analyzing reading logs, and using findings to adjust program delivery in real time. These experiences directly inform the design and evaluation plan for Family Literacy Circles.

Two committed partners support program delivery. Riverview East Elementary School provides meeting space, enrollment referrals, and student attendance data under a signed data-sharing agreement. Westside Community Library hosts circle sessions, provides childcare space, and supports community outreach. Both partnerships are documented in signed MOUs and letters of support submitted with this application.

Community Literacy Collaborative maintains strong fiscal and compliance systems. We undergo an annual independent audit, carry appropriate insurance, and use established payroll and financial management systems. In recent years, we have managed multiple public and foundation grants with monthly budget-to-actual tracking, timely reporting, and no material audit findings.

Looking ahead, we are building a sustainable funding base for Family Literacy Circles beyond this grant. We are actively pursuing local foundation support, individual giving, and public funding opportunities. The peer parent leader pipeline built into the program model reduces long-term staffing costs by training program graduates to co-facilitate future circles. Partner in-kind contributions for meeting space and hosting further reduce the cost of ongoing delivery. Together, these strategies position the program to continue serving families after the grant period ends.
